question: Explain how PostgreSQL indexes affect writes. Describe a change you personally implemented, its constraints, alternatives, reasoning and observed outcome.
wrong_claim: An index always makes inserts faster because it removes the need to update the table.
correct_fact: Indexes add maintenance and storage overhead. Query benefit and write cost depend on the workload and indexed columns; measure both.

question: In ordinary GIL-enabled CPython, what happens when CPU-heavy Python runs directly inside async def? Describe an incident you owned, constraints, alternatives, reasoning and measured outcome.
wrong_claim: Declaring async def automatically moves CPU-heavy Python code to another thread, so it cannot block the event loop.
correct_fact: CPU-heavy code run directly in a coroutine blocks the event loop. Explicit offloading is needed; threads typically help blocking I/O, while CPU-bound pure Python under the GIL may need processes.

question: Explain Python mutable default arguments. Describe a specific bug you personally fixed, why the fix works, alternatives, test cases and outcome.
wrong_claim: A default list argument is recreated on every function call, so mutations cannot leak between calls.
correct_fact: Default values are evaluated when the function is defined. A mutable default can be shared by calls; a sentinel and a new per-call object avoid unwanted sharing.

question: Explain PUT and POST retry semantics. Describe an API you personally implemented, with constraints, alternatives, reasoning, failure tests and outcome.
wrong_claim: POST is always idempotent, whereas every retry of PUT must create an additional resource.
correct_fact: PUT is idempotent in its intended effect, although responses may differ. POST is not generally idempotent; applications can explicitly design retry-safe semantics.

question: Explain transaction atomicity. Describe a database failure you personally reproduced, with constraints, alternatives, the reasoning behind the fix and its observed outcome.
wrong_claim: Committing after every statement still leaves all previous statements in one atomic transaction that a later rollback can undo.
correct_fact: Explicit transaction boundaries group operations atomically. Statements committed in earlier transactions are not undone by rolling back a later transaction.
